newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES LITTLE MOVED ON THURSDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES LITTLE MOVED ON THURSDAY.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were on Thursday hovering around their previous levels in fairly quiet trade, dealers said.
The market opened with a surplus of Z$73 million and further liquidity was added with the maturity of about Z$150 million worth of treasury bills.

The Reserve Bank as a result auctioned treasury bills amounting to Z$200 million with an average yield of 22.98 percent, slightly above Wednesday's 22.96 percent. Call money added two-and-a-half percentage points to 22.5 percent.
NCD bills with 30-, 60- and 90-day maturities were quoted unchanged at 24 percent (buying) while their selling rate eased slightly to 23 percent from 23.5.
Bankers acceptances were being bought and sold at 23.5 and 22.75 percent respectively, little changed from 23.5 and 22.5 percent.
